sources.title: India, Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas: World Heritage nomination dossier
sources.note: Direct full dossier: printed pages 100 to 101, Somanathapura foundation, endowments and learning; page 121 Hoysala decline. Nomination and derived UNESCO statement grouped as one work. The dossier incorrectly names Ballala II beside its 1300 inscription; that regnal attribution is not repeated. Its categorical 1343 dynasty ending is qualified using Kasdorf’s 1346 political endpoint.

sources.title: UNESCO, Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple: description and Statement of Outstanding Universal Value
sources.note: Direct original statement: construction from 1213, lightweight brick roofing, carved dolerite, reservoir and irrigation landscape. Nomination and derived statement treated as one work. No modern earthquake-proof guarantee adopted.

sources.title: Katherine E. Kasdorf, Hoysaleshvara temple, Halebidu (2021)
sources.note: Full original indexed text recovered with exact title and Kalidasi query; direct fetch fails. Author’s archaeological/art-historical analysis and photographs. Sections A double temple to Shiva and Detailed sculpture, introduction gives political period circa 1000 to 1346. Khan Academy mirror counted as same work.

sources.title: Dominik Wujastyk, The Evidence for Hospitals in Early India, History of Science in South Asia 10 (2022), 1 to 43
sources.note: Direct full article, printed page 28, section 12, exact Sanskrit Roman forms ārogyaśālā and prasūtiśāla with translations. Article dates Malkapuram 1286, whereas epigraphic catalogue and Rama Rao date main grant 1261. Public witness is consequently dated only thirteenth century; no reconstructed ancient script, treatment outcomes or hygienic layout asserted.

sources.title: Dr. MCR HRD Institute, epigraphic compilation, Volume II: Kakatiya inscriptions
sources.note: Direct full government compilation, entry 300 printed pages 311 to 312: Malkapuram main grant catalogued 25 March 1261; source South Indian Inscriptions X, pages 205 to 209. Entry 194, pages 227 to 229, reproduces Hultzsch’s Motupalli edict study, dated 1244 to 1245. Statements about caste-inclusive feeding are documented institutional provisions, not proof of universal social equality.

sources.title: B. Rama Rao, Medical Allusions in Some Inscriptions of Andhra Pradesh, Bulletin of the Indian Institute of History of Medicine, volume V
sources.note: Direct eleven-page article. Printed pages 200 to 201: Malkapuram pillar, 200 lines and Sanskrit verse with Telugu boundary information; financing and shares. Printed page 203, section 6: Palakol horse physician Vasudeva and father Anantapandita, 1300. Author’s speculation about fully equipped hospitals is not adopted.

sources.note: Official original indexed historical introduction verifies the Delhi expedition’s conquest of Warangal in 1323 and Prataparudra’s captivity. Only those basic events are used; dated colonial-style judgments and later legendary genealogies in the digest are not adopted.

proposedOverrides.name: Regional kingdoms of medieval India
proposedOverrides.summary: An atlas umbrella combining unrelated island fragments with regional Indian kingdoms.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Separate regional-context card, no associations with the other two superficially similar umbrella IDs.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 1279 combines India, Borneo and southwestern Sulawesi. 1300 retains only India. No claim that these components were one political or religious entity.
batchIdentityNotes.historicalScope: Named Hoysala and Kakatiya examples in and around the Indian polygon, with clearly flagged earlier foundations and nearby comparisons. Specific dynasties, ancient Hindu Kingdoms and Rajput umbrella dossiers remain separate.
dateDiscrepancies: Malkapuram main grant 1261 in epigraphic catalogue and Rama Rao versus 1286 in Wujastyk: exact writing sample dated thirteenth century only.
Hoysala nomination incorrectly associates 1300 with Ballala II; no ruler name repeated.
Nomination dates Hoysala ending 1343 while Kasdorf gives 1346; public ending uses 1340s.
